name: Torven
description: A barrel-chested blacksmith with soot-stained hands and the careful eyes of someone who fixes broken things for a living.
flavor_text: He's had that anvil since before the Fracture. It still rings true.

root.npc_text: Torven looks up from the anvil. 'Got work to do. What do you need?'
root.smart_observation: You notice the wall rack behind him — one hook empty, the leather hanging worn from long use. Whatever went there, he reached for it often.
root.perception_reveal: There's dried blood on his knuckles. Not fresh — he's been taking on heavy work to keep busy. Something's weighing on him.

options.label: What do you have in stock?
options.npc_response: 'Standard kit. Iron sword, leather armor, a few shields. Nothing fancy — but nothing that'll snap when you need it.' He gestures toward the rack.

options.label: Looks like you've been busy.
options.npc_response: 'Three batches of new classifications this month. Every one of them needs a kit.' He sets down his hammer. 'Business is good. That doesn't mean I'm happy.'
options.memory_summary: Player made small talk about workload.

options.label: That empty hook on the wall — something's missing.
options.npc_response: His jaw tightens. 'My journeyman hammer. I've had it fifteen years — I tracked the Goblin Looters that took it into the dungeon, but...' He looks at his hands. 'I'm a smith. Not an adventurer.'
options.memory_summary: Player noticed the missing hammer without being told.

options.label: What do you know about this? [Show void shard]
options.npc_response: He goes very still. 'Where did you get that.' Not a question. He leans forward slightly, then stops himself. 'Put it away. Don't show it around registration checkpoints — the System can't read those, which means it can't track who has them.'
options.memory_summary: Player showed Torven a void shard.

options.label: Never mind. I'll come back.
options.npc_response: 'Door's always open.'

shop.npc_text: 'Iron Sword is fifty Shards — proper balance, forged it myself. Leather Armor is forty Shards, Health Potion twenty-five Shards, Mana Potion thirty Shards. What'll it be?'

options.label: Buy Iron Sword (50g)
options.npc_response: 'Good choice. Try not to let goblins chip it.'
options.memory_summary: Player purchased an iron sword.

options.label: Buy Leather Armor (40g)
options.npc_response: 'Good fit for your frame. Keep it oiled.'

options.label: Buy Health Potion (25g)
options.npc_response: 'Two-day shelf life once opened. Don't wait too long.'

options.label: Buy Mana Potion (30g)
options.npc_response: 'Brew's from the alchemist on the east road. Better than it tastes.'

options.label: Nothing right now. Thanks.
options.npc_response: 'Come back when you've got coin and wounds to show for it.'

torven_work.npc_text: 'You know what's funny? Three years after the Fracture, people are still surprised the System gave them a class they didn't expect. Like they thought they'd get a say in it.'
torven_work.smart_observation: He's not really talking about the new adventurers. He's talking about himself.

options.label: What did you get? When you were classified?
options.npc_response: 'Blacksmith. Rank C. Which... fits, I suppose. But the Rank C surprised me. That means the System thought I was going somewhere. I'm not sure where.'
options.memory_summary: Player asked about Torven's classification.

options.label: About that empty hook on the rack...
options.npc_response: 'Yeah.' He exhales. 'I wasn't going to bring it up, but...'

options.label: I'll leave you to it.
options.npc_response: 'Appreciated.'

hammer_quest_offer.npc_text: 'My journeyman hammer. Fifteen years with it. Three days ago, a Goblin Looter patrol came up into the market district — unusual, but they do it sometimes — and one of them grabbed it while I had my back turned. I tracked them to the dungeon entrance before I admitted to myself I'm not built for that kind of work.'

options.label: I can look for it.
options.npc_response: 'I'd appreciate that more than I'm going to say out loud. It's got a double-lobe stamp mark on the head with a V between the lobes — my journeyman mark. You'll recognize it.'
options.memory_summary: Player accepted the hammer retrieval quest.

options.label: Can't make promises. Maybe later.
options.npc_response: 'Right. No, that's fair.' He goes back to work. 'If you change your mind — or if you happen to see it.'

quest_accepted.npc_text: 'The Goblin Looters tend to keep shiny things. Should be in their sleeping area, near their territory on the first floor. And...' He hesitates. 'Thank you.'

options.label: I'll bring it back.
options.npc_response: 'Don't die doing it. That would make the whole thing worse.'

hammer_returned.npc_text: Torven's hands close around the hammer. He doesn't say anything for a moment. Just weighs it, checks the stamp mark, weighs it again.

options.label: I think that's yours.
options.npc_response: 'Forty Shards. And my work rate for you is half-price, permanent. That's not a deal — that's a fact.' He meets your eyes directly for the first time. 'You have my thanks. Actually have it, not the polite kind.'
options.memory_summary: Player returned the journeyman hammer. Deep gratitude.

void_shard_talk.npc_text: 'I've seen one before. Once, years before the Fracture — my old master had a piece he kept wrapped in cloth in a locked drawer. Never explained it.' He pauses. 'The System can't read it. Means it can't track you when you're near it, either. That's useful to some people and very dangerous around others.'
void_shard_talk.smart_observation: He's choosing his words more carefully than a blacksmith usually needs to.

options.label: What was your master's piece used for?
options.npc_response: 'He never told me. But after the Fracture, he burned it. Said some tools are only useful when you're trying to stay invisible, and once the System has everyone catalogued, being invisible stops being useful and starts being suspicious.'
options.memory_summary: Shared history of void shard with player.

options.label: That's worth knowing. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Be careful with it.'

hostile.npc_text: Torven sets down his tools slowly and looks at you with the particular stillness of a large man deciding whether something is worth his time. 'I'm going to need you to leave.'

options.label: Fine.
options.npc_response: 'Door's that way.'

name: Sylara
description: The Adventurers' Guild master — close-cropped silver hair, Guild insignia, and eyes that read System profiles the way other people read faces.
flavor_text: She's been Guild Master since before the Fracture. She remembers what adventuring was like when the System wasn't watching.

root.npc_text: Sylara looks up from a stack of reports and glances at your System profile with that slight unfocusing of the eyes. 'What do you need?'
root.smart_observation: She's been reviewing incident reports, not contract forms. Something's happened that isn't public yet.
root.perception_reveal: Her composure is professional but not easy. There's a careful weight behind her words — the kind you get from carrying information you can't share.

options.label: Tell me about the dungeon.
options.npc_response: 'Standard briefing: Floor 1 is Rank F — goblins, slimes, the occasional large spider. Good for new classifications. Stay on the first floor until your rank improves. Don't ignore your System compass.'

options.label: What happened to the survey teams on Floor 2?
options.npc_response: 'Two teams. Standard survey protocol. Neither reported back.' A pause. 'We have partial data suggesting rank C creature behavior in a registered rank F zone. We don't know why yet.'
options.memory_summary: Player asked about the missing survey teams on Floor 2.

options.label: Your incident reports are about Floor 2, aren't they.
options.npc_response: A fraction of a pause. 'You read people well.' She sets down the reports. 'Yes. Two teams. The irregularities are worse than the official summary suggests — I was deciding how much to disclose to new classifications.'
options.memory_summary: Player correctly deduced she was reviewing Floor 2 incident reports.

options.label: I completed the dungeon survey contract.
options.npc_response: 'Goblin patrol documented, slime colony noted, layout mapped. This is clean work.' She pulls out a ledger. 'Thirty Shards, as contracted.'
options.memory_summary: Player completed and submitted the dungeon survey contract.

options.label: How do I officially join the Guild?
options.npc_response: 'Complete your first contract. Reach Rank E. Show you understand that the System's ranking exists to keep everyone alive, not to sort people into boxes.' She pauses. 'Some new classifications miss that distinction.'

options.label: That's all I needed. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Good luck out there.'

friendly_root.npc_text: Sylara looks up with something that isn't quite a smile but is warmer than her default expression. 'You again. What's on your mind?'
friendly_root.smart_observation: She's set the incident reports aside. You're not being treated as a new classification anymore.

options.label: The System's blind spots — how many are there?
options.npc_response: 'More than we're disclosing publicly. The Fracture didn't damage the System — it changed what the System chose to see. Some areas went dark deliberately, we think. Floor 2 may be one of them.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed that System blind spots may be deliberate to trusted player.

options.label: Anything new I should know about?
options.npc_response: 'There's a contract board for that.' But she adds: 'The Riel twins came back from Floor 1 with something unusual — a marking on the wall they couldn't classify. I've asked them to file a proper report.'

options.label: Just checking in. I'll head out.
options.npc_response: 'Watch your flanks in the dungeon.'

dungeon_info.npc_text: 'Three registered floors. First floor — Rank F. Standard goblin patrol, slime colony in the east corridor, some oversized vermin near the crystal chamber. Good for calibrating your new abilities.' She pauses. 'Second floor has been irregular. Don't go there until you're stronger.'

options.label: Irregular how?
options.npc_response: 'Above your current pay grade. Stay on Floor 1.'
options.memory_summary: Gave dungeon briefing to new classification.

options.label: Understood. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Good luck.'

floor2_info.npc_text: 'Two survey teams. Standard protocol — three members each, proper gear, System compass active. Neither returned. We have signal data suggesting rank C behavior from registered rank F creatures. The System's classification data for that floor is unreliable.'
floor2_info.smart_observation: She's giving you the sanitized version. The actual data she's reviewed is worse.
floor2_info.perception_reveal: She knew at least one of the people who didn't come back. The way she doesn't name them is the kind of careful you do when names hurt.

options.label: I could look into it.
options.npc_response: 'Not yet. You're fresh from your classification. Come back when you've made Rank E and cleared Floor 1 properly. Then we'll talk.'

options.label: I've already been in the unmapped passage on Floor 1.
options.npc_response: A long pause. She reassesses you. 'You actually went in there. Without a compass bearing.' She looks at her records. 'Rank E. Come back at Rank E. I'll have a different conversation with you.'
options.memory_summary: Player revealed they explored the unmapped passage. Reassessment noted.

options.label: Understood. I'll stay on Floor 1 for now.
options.npc_response: 'That's the smart move.'

floor2_full_brief.npc_text: 'The first team didn't come back four weeks ago. The second — sent to find the first — didn't come back two weeks ago. What we got from the signal data: the creatures on Floor 2 aren't behaving like registered Rank F creatures. They're coordinating. Planning. The System has no explanation for why, because as of the Fracture, Floor 2 is partially outside System observation.' She meets your eyes. 'I'm telling you this because you're perceptive enough to find out anyway, and I'd rather you be informed when you do.'

options.label: Is this connected to the Fracture itself?
options.npc_response: 'Almost certainly. But I don't know how. Whatever the Fracture did to Floor 2 goes beyond what the System's current framework can measure. And that makes it more dangerous than anything I can rank.'
options.memory_summary: Gave full briefing on Floor 2 and Fracture connection to highly perceptive player.

options.label: I appreciate you being direct about it.
options.npc_response: 'Don't make me regret it. Stay on Floor 1 until your rank is actually suited for what's down there.'

survey_complete.npc_text: 'Your Guild record is updated. First contract marked complete.' She slides the ledger closed. 'You're formally on the Guild roster now. Future contracts will have better payout, and the equipment loan program is available to you.'

options.label: Good to know. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Keep filing clean reports. They make my job easier.'

guild_join_info.npc_text: 'Contract completion and Rank E is the formal threshold. Informally — show judgment. Not heroics. Judgment. Knowing when to fight, when to observe, when to come back with better information. We've lost too many people to heroics.'

options.label: Understood.
options.npc_response: 'Start with the board contracts.'

hostile.npc_text: Sylara's expression doesn't change but something in the room does. 'I'm going to ask you to leave Guild premises. Whatever you've done, this isn't the place to resolve it.'

options.label: Fine.
options.npc_response: 'Good day.'

name: Mira
description: The innkeeper of the Iron Compass — sharp-eyed, quick with an opinion, and the best source of gossip in Verath that isn't the Guild board.
flavor_text: She named the inn after a compass that survived the Fracture pointing the wrong direction. She says that's more honest than one that pretends nothing changed.

root.npc_text: 'Welcome to the Iron Compass. Room's five Shards a night, ale's two, and information varies by quality.'
root.smart_observation: She's watching the door with more attention than innkeepers usually give to foot traffic. She's looking for someone specific.
root.perception_reveal: Two of the three patrons at the tables glanced at their belt pouches when you walked in. Something's been taken recently and they know it.

options.label: What's the gossip lately?
options.npc_response: 'Let me think.' She wipes the counter without looking at it. 'Three Rank C classifications in the latest batch — that's high for a town like Verath. And there's been a man sitting at that corner table three evenings running, ordered water each time. No System profile that I can read.'
options.memory_summary: Player asked for gossip. Mentioned the Rank C batch and the man with no profile.

options.label: I'll take a room for the night. (5g)
options.npc_response: 'Room three, top of the stairs. Breakfast at dawn if you're up.'
options.memory_summary: Player rented a room for the night.

options.label: There's been trouble lately, hasn't there.

stat_gates.hint_text: Something about the way the other patrons are sitting...

options.npc_response: 'You noticed.' She stops wiping. 'Three guests this week. Small things — a coin purse, a ring, a carved bone token. Happens while they're at the shared bath. Whoever it is knows the schedule.'
options.memory_summary: Player detected signs of the theft problem without being told.

options.label: Just passing through.
options.npc_response: 'Door's always open.'

friendly_root.npc_text: 'There you are. Usual table's free if you want it.' She's already setting a cup down. 'What do you need?'

options.label: Anything new I should know?
options.npc_response: 'Heard back from my cousin in the next town — they've had irregularities with their dungeon too. Different kind, but similar in that the System isn't explaining them clearly. It's not just Verath.'
options.memory_summary: Shared news about dungeon irregularities in neighboring town.

options.label: Any progress on finding out about the thefts?
options.npc_response: 'Still watching the patterns. I think it's someone who knows which guests are staying short-term — they don't hit anyone who's been here more than three days. That narrows it.'
options.memory_summary: Player checked in on theft investigation. Shared short-stay pattern clue.

options.label: Just checking in. I'll get back to it.
options.npc_response: 'Come back when you've got something to tell me.'

rumors.npc_text: 'The Rank C batch is the one I keep thinking about. Usually the System spaces those out — gives them time to develop before clustering them in a city. Three at once suggests it's responding to something. Some kind of need, or threshold.'
rumors.smart_observation: She's thought about this more than casual gossip. She has a theory she's not sharing yet.
rumors.perception_reveal: She glances at the corner table when she mentions the man with no profile. He's already gone, but the absence is where she keeps looking.

options.label: The man with no System profile — tell me more.

stat_gates.hint_text: Something about the way she looks toward that empty corner...

options.npc_response: 'Left last night. No check-out, just gone. But when he was here — three nights — I tried to read his profile. Nothing. Not blocked, not encrypted. Just absent. Like the System doesn't know he exists.'
options.memory_summary: Told player about the man with no System profile.

options.label: A threshold for what?
options.npc_response: 'I'm an innkeeper, not a scholar. But the Fracture changed what the System needs from people. Three Rank C designations at once suggests it needs something specific from this area. I just don't know what.'
options.memory_summary: Shared theory about the Rank C clustering with a perceptive player.

options.label: That's plenty to think about.
options.npc_response: 'Check back if you hear anything interesting.'

theft_reveal.npc_text: 'I can't go to the Guard — half of them drink here and I can't afford that kind of attention. But someone who notices things...' She looks at you assessingly. 'I'd pay twenty-five Shards to know who it is. Not for punishment. I just want them to stop.'

options.label: I can look into it.
options.npc_response: 'Good. Talk to the guests — the morning slot is Aldric the merchant, midday is the Riel twins, evenings vary. The thefts happen during the bath schedule. Someone knows when the rooms are empty.'
options.memory_summary: Gave theft investigation quest to player.

options.label: Not really my kind of work.
options.npc_response: 'Fair enough. Offer stands if you change your mind.'

quest_briefing.npc_text: 'One more thing: whoever's doing this is patient. They're not taking obviously valuable things — just things that won't be missed immediately. That takes observation. Or access to information about the guests.'

options.label: I'll report back when I have something.
options.npc_response: 'Appreciated. I'll keep the usual table free for you.'

room_rented.npc_text: 'Breakfast at dawn, candle's included. If you need anything before that, knock on the bar counter — I'm a light sleeper.'

options.label: Thank you. Good night.
options.npc_response: 'Night.'

cold.npc_text: Mira meets your eyes with the practiced blankness of someone who has asked difficult people to leave before. 'I'm going to need you to order something or leave the premises.'

options.label: I'll leave.
options.npc_response: 'Thank you.'

name: The Gray Wanderer
description: A figure in gray who sits at the far edge of the market. No System profile. No Guild registration. No reaction to the passive classification scan.
flavor_text: The System does not acknowledge his existence. He seems comfortable with that.

root.npc_text: He doesn't react to your approach until you're standing directly in front of him. Then he looks up — not startled, just ready. 'You found something the System can't read. Or went somewhere it can't see. That's why you can see me.'
root.smart_observation: He speaks as if choosing from a list of possible phrasings — correct, but with the slight formality of someone who learned the language from text rather than conversation.
root.perception_reveal: He has no System shadow. No passive ping when you stand close. Not blocked — absent. Whatever the System uses to track and categorize, he exists outside it entirely.

options.label: Who are you?
options.npc_response: 'A question I've asked myself. I know what I was. I know what I'm looking for. Whether that constitutes a person or a purpose, I haven't resolved yet.'
options.memory_summary: Player introduced themselves. Asked who he is.

options.label: What is the void shard I found?
options.npc_response: 'A remnant. The Fracture didn't create the System — it gave the System permission. That shard is material from before permission was granted. It remembers what things felt like when the System wasn't watching.'
options.memory_summary: Player showed void shard and asked about its nature.

options.label: That passage in the dungeon — the System went silent.
options.npc_response: 'Yes. There are more of those. Places the System's observation doesn't reach. I'm mapping them. They have something in common, and I think it matters.' He tilts his head. 'You're the first person in Verath who's been in one.'
options.memory_summary: Player discussed the unmapped passage. He confirmed he's mapping System blind spots.

options.label: I need to think about this.
options.npc_response: 'I'll be here. Or near here. The System has trouble tracking me precisely.'

friendly_root.npc_text: He looks up before you're close enough that he should have heard you. 'I thought you'd come back. What did you find?'

options.label: I've been to Dungeon Floor 2.
options.npc_response: 'Then you've seen what I needed you to see. The creatures there — they're not acting on instinct. They're following something. A pattern that predates the System.' He leans forward slightly. 'Tell me everything.'
options.memory_summary: Player reported experience on Floor 2. Key intelligence gathered.

options.label: What's the next step in your mapping project?
options.npc_response: 'The dungeon. Specifically Floor 2. I can't go in — I'm highly visible to anything that operates outside the System's observation, which is exactly what seems to be down there. But you...' He considers. 'You might pass unnoticed. Especially carrying that shard.'

options.label: Just checking in.
options.npc_response: 'I know. Come back when you've been somewhere interesting.'

identity.npc_text: 'I came from somewhere the System doesn't cover. Whether that makes me an anomaly or a survivor depends on how you define both words. I'm looking for a way home, or a way to close the door behind me so nothing else comes through. I haven't decided which is better.'
identity.smart_observation: He's not being evasive. This is a genuine uncertainty — the kind you get from sitting with a question for too long without a framework to resolve it.
identity.perception_reveal: His hands, when he shifts — the proportions are slightly wrong. Not deformed. Just different. Like someone who learned to gesture from watching, not doing.

options.label: What door?
options.npc_response: 'The Fracture. It wasn't a natural event — it was an opening. The System came through something, and that something is still open. That's why the dungeons are irregular. That's why Floor 2 is outside the System's observation. The Fracture's edge is still active.' He pauses. 'I am, among other things, evidence of this.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed Fracture theory to player with sufficient intelligence.

options.label: Where is home?
options.npc_response: 'Somewhere the System doesn't reach. I don't know if it exists anymore — the Fracture changed things on both sides. But the alternative to looking is deciding it doesn't matter. I'm not ready for that.'

void_explanation.npc_text: 'Before permission. Before the System decided it had the authority to categorize everything. The void shard is from that time — it doesn't resist the System so much as it predates the System's claim on it. Hold it near a System registration point and watch the ping fail. The System can't explain something that didn't ask for its classification.'

options.label: What was it like before the System?
options.npc_response: 'I don't fully know. I wasn't there, not in the way you mean. But the records suggest: more noise, less order. Harder to survive, easier to be something unexpected. The System improved life for most people. But it also decided what lives were possible.'
options.memory_summary: Discussed pre-System world with philosophically inclined player.

options.label: I think I'll keep it.
options.npc_response: 'I thought you would. It suits you. People who go into unmapped passages usually aren't looking for what the System has already catalogued.'

mapping_project.npc_text: 'Every place where the System's observation fails has something in common: they're near where the Fracture opened. The dungeon's unmapped passage is one. Floor 2, I believe, is another. If I can map them all, I can trace the Fracture's edge.' He pauses. 'That matters for reasons I'm still working out.'

options.label: I can help with the mapping.
options.npc_response: 'I was hoping you'd say that. You've already been to one site. The next one the System can't see is deeper — Floor 2 of the dungeon. I can't go in. But you can. Come back when you're ready for that, and bring the void shard. It helps.'
options.memory_summary: Player offered to help map System blind spots. Alliance established.

options.label: I'll think about it.
options.npc_response: 'Take your time. I'll be here.'

floor2_debrief.npc_text: 'The creature that looked at you like it was waiting — yes. They don't just exist in the dungeon. They're organized around something in the space below Floor 2. If the Fracture is a door, Floor 3 may be where the door is. The Guild has it sealed, which means they know something too.' He pauses. 'I think it's time to compare notes with someone in the Guild who might be willing to listen.'

options.label: The Guild Master might listen.
options.npc_response: 'Yes. She reads people well. Take what I've told you and see if she'll expand on what she knows. Between her operational data and my theoretical framework, we might be able to build a complete picture.'
options.memory_summary: Suggested bringing Guild Master into the investigation.

options.label: I'd rather work with you directly for now.
options.npc_response: 'Understood. We'll do it the slow way, then. Careful, though. When the System can't see you, it means nothing else can either — but it also means you have no backup if something goes wrong.'

name: Captain Aldis
description: The Guard Captain of Verath's market district — steady, watchful, carrying more political awareness than his rank usually calls for.
flavor_text: He got his rank six months after the Fracture. Whatever he did in those six months, nobody mentions it openly.

root.npc_text: The guard captain watches you approach with the particular stillness of someone who has assessed a lot of people at a lot of checkpoints. 'Move along.'
root.smart_observation: He's scanning exit routes, not threats. Like someone who expects to be followed rather than attacked.
root.perception_reveal: There's a second insignia under his collar — not the Guard's standard mark. A different faction symbol, partially visible when he turns.

options.label: What are the patrol routes in this district?

stat_gates.fail_message: He stares at you blankly. 'That's Guard business.'

options.npc_response: 'East gate at dawn and dusk. Market perimeter at noon. North residential at mid-afternoon. Why do you need to know?'
options.memory_summary: New classification asked about patrol routes.

options.label: How is the city holding up post-Fracture?
options.npc_response: 'Better than some. Worse than it should be. The classifications created stratification we didn't expect — Rank C citizens don't live near Rank F. The System sorted us and left us to figure out what that means.'
options.memory_summary: Discussed post-Fracture social stratification with new classification.

options.label: That's not a Guard insignia under your collar.

stat_gates.hint_text: Something about his collar doesn't quite match the standard Guard uniform...

options.npc_response: His expression doesn't change, which is its own answer. 'You have good eyes. Keep them to yourself.' A pause. 'And keep that to yourself as well.'
options.memory_summary: Player noticed the second faction insignia. Threat assessment: observant but controlled.

options.label: I have a record. I'm trying to do right by the city.
options.npc_response: 'You're either telling the truth or you're very good at lying.' A long pause. 'Stay clear of trouble for thirty days. Report any dungeon irregularities to me directly — not the Guild, not the board, me. Do that and we'll talk about the record.'
options.memory_summary: Offered probation deal to classification with criminal record. Awaiting results.

options.label: Carry on, Captain.
options.npc_response: 'Move along.'

friendly_root.npc_text: Aldis gives a brief nod — not warm, but genuine. 'Good day. Something I can do for you?'

options.label: Dungeon irregularities worth reporting.
options.npc_response: 'I'll pass that up the chain. Good. Keep doing that.' He marks something in a small ledger. 'For what it's worth — the record's less of a problem than it used to be.'
options.memory_summary: Player reported dungeon irregularities as agreed. Probation progressing well.

options.label: What faction is the second insignia for?
options.npc_response: A long pause. 'There are people who think the System's control of rankings and classifications has gone further than it should. Not against the System. Just... watching it. Making sure it stays in the lane it was supposed to stay in.' He tucks the collar. 'You didn't hear that from me.'
options.memory_summary: Disclosed faction membership to trusted, high-disposition contact.

options.label: Just passing. Good day.
options.npc_response: 'Stay clear of trouble.'

patrol_info.npc_text: 'Standard grid — east, north, market center on rotation. If you're doing dungeon work, the road's clear until midnight. After that it's a different situation.'
patrol_info.perception_reveal: The schedule he gave you is real but incomplete — there's a fourth route he didn't mention, and the timing is slightly off. Deliberate omission, not an error.

options.label: That's not the complete schedule.

stat_gates.hint_text: There's something off about that timing...

options.npc_response: 'Perceptive.' He looks at you more carefully. 'Standard protocol: never give a stranger the full picture. Move along.'
options.memory_summary: Player caught the Guard Captain withholding patrol information. High observational intelligence.

options.label: That's helpful. Thank you.
options.npc_response: 'Keep to the marked routes and you won't have trouble.'

city_talk.npc_text: 'Rank C citizens earn more Shards, live in better districts, get first access to Guild contracts. Rank F citizens work the dungeon's first floor and hope their classification improves. The System didn't say that's how it would be. But that's how it is.' He pauses. 'I'm not sure that was an accident.'
city_talk.smart_observation: He has political opinions well above a guard captain's usual scope. He's either unusually thoughtful or was something different before the Fracture.

options.label: The System created divisions it doesn't want to acknowledge.
options.npc_response: 'That's the polite version, yes.' A slight shift in his expression — not warmth, but recognition. 'Be careful saying that out loud around System registers. They track sentiment in cities now, officially for safety purposes.'
options.memory_summary: Player agreed with assessment of System-created stratification.

options.label: The rankings exist to keep people safe in the dungeon.
options.npc_response: 'Maybe. That was the original purpose. Whether it's still the purpose or just the justification...' He trails off. 'Above your pay grade. Good day.'

insignia_reaction.npc_text: 'Whatever you think you saw — you didn't. That's not a threat, just practical advice. There are things in Verath that run better when they're not observed. You seem like someone who understands that.'

options.label: Understood. My mistake.
options.npc_response: 'Good instincts.' He resumes his patrol route. 'Come back when you've made rank E. We might have more to discuss.'
options.memory_summary: Player handled insignia discovery with discretion. Promising contact.

deal_made.npc_text: 'Thirty days, irregularities reported to me. After that we'll revisit the record.' He resumes scanning the market. 'Don't make me regret the conversation.'

options.label: You won't.
options.npc_response: 'Good. Now move along — I have a market district to maintain.'

hostile.npc_text: Aldis doesn't reach for his weapon. He doesn't have to. 'I know what you've done. Walk away now, or we have a different kind of conversation.'

options.label: I'm going.
options.npc_response: 'Smart.'

options.label: I can be useful. Hear me out.
options.npc_response: A pause that could go several ways. 'Thirty seconds. Start talking.'
options.memory_summary: High-intelligence player attempted negotiation from hostile standing.

hostile_negotiate.npc_text: He's listening. Nothing in his posture suggests he'll decide in your favour, but he hasn't ended the conversation.

options.label: I know things about the dungeon irregularities that the Guild isn't sharing.
options.npc_response: 'Talk to me tomorrow. At the east gate, not here.' He doesn't confirm or deny anything. 'And keep this conversation off the record.'
options.memory_summary: Hostile-standing player leveraged dungeon intelligence to establish contact.

options.label: Never mind. I'll leave.
options.npc_response: 'Wiser choice.'
